newsitem.title: UK: GEC to link with Fiat for rail bid - paper.
newsitem.headline: GEC to link with Fiat for rail bid - paper.

text.p: Britain's General Electric Co Plc is to form an alliance with Italy's Fiat SpA to bid for the contract to build trains for the West Coast line linking London and Glasgow, a report in the Independent newspaper said.

The 600-million-pound ($958.2 million) contract will include a new generation of tilting trains and is expected to create 5,000 jobs in Britain, the report said, adding that Fiat had already made tilting trains for Italy, Switzerland and Finland.
No one at GEC could be reached for comment.

Rival Adtranz, a merger of the rail units of Germany's Daimler-Benz and Swiss-Swedish ABB, last September unveiled a family of tilting trains, saying the West Coast route would be an ideal start for its marketing efforts for the train.
Adtranz said the train could cut the journey time between London and Glasgow from five hours to four.
